# sgen010 — DepMap 26Q3 metadata discriminator (ledger-first SPEC)

Locked before any probing, 2026-10-29. Inputs are the two user-supplied metadata
files only; neither contains dependency outcomes.

## Inputs (hashes recorded at acquisition)
- data/Model.csv — sha256 65eb1895800e71a963a3ab56e5d08c8d006cb0d9e7aa68f7e34a3810a2a3cbc7 (789,805 bytes; copied from ~/Downloads, source hash identical)
- data/CRISPRScreenMap.csv — sha256 43cc528614053d4c5a96729c2d782375227231a0cfea23de6c519b8989fa1252 (41,721 bytes; copied from ~/Downloads, source hash identical)
- lock_s/cohort.csv (locked; 148 models, donor_ID = COSMIC individual_ID)
- generations/sgen001/identity_reconciliation_v1.json (142 Passports patients authoritative)

## Question
Does DepMap 26Q3 metadata identify a CRISPR-screened model pool that is
(a) countable at patient level (PatientID present), and (b) donor-disjoint from
the 148-model / 142-patient spent external cohort C on every available join key?
If yes, how large is the disjoint screened pool, at model and patient level?

## Method (metadata only; no outcome access)
1. Model.csv: row count, distinct PatientID, GrowthPattern / ModelType /
   DepmapModelType distributions; 3D/organoid-class subset counts.
2. CRISPRScreenMap.csv: screen count, distinct screened ModelID; inner join to
   Model.csv -> screened patients.
3. Donor disjointness vs cohort C on every candidate key present in both:
   cohort donor_ID vs Model COSMICID; cohort model names (from identity
   reconciliation) vs CellLineName/StrippedCellLineName; cohort sample_ID
   prefixes vs any Model identifier column. Report each overlap separately.
   A model counts as C-overlapping if ANY key matches (conservative union).
4. Disjoint screened pool = screened models minus union-overlap models; report
   model count and distinct-patient count. Also report disjoint screened
   patients (a patient is excluded if ANY of their models overlaps C).

## Decision rule (fixed before probing)
- POOL_IDENTIFIED: disjoint screened pool >= 100 models AND >= 100 patients
  (a fresh patient-level biological evaluation is at least structurally
  possible; power/endpoint design is a later generation).
- POOL_TOO_SMALL: otherwise.
Either verdict is a used discriminator result. No outcome file is downloaded,
opened, or referenced by this generation.

## Failure modes named in advance
- Join keys may not connect (DepMap COSMICID is a sample-level ID; cohort
  donor_ID is individual-level): then disjointness rests on name keys only and
  the verdict must say so.
- PatientID missingness in Model.csv shrinks the countable pool.

## Amendment (2026-10-29, before v3 probing)
v1 keys did not connect. v2 Passports HCMI bridge covered 48/148 models
(50/142 patients) -> POOL_IDENTIFIED_BRIDGE_PARTIAL. v3 completes the bridge
locally by reproducing pgen003 Witness A exactly (normalized
model_name+synonyms join of cohort sample_IDs on the same
passports_model_list_20260921.csv; pgen003 reported 148/148 resolved, 142
patients, 0 multi-patient). v3 must independently reproduce those counts
before using the patient set; exclusion then = every Passports model of the
142 C patients (SIDM / BROAD_ID / COSMIC_ID / names) joined to DepMap
Model.csv. Decision rule and thresholds unchanged. No network, no outcomes.

## Amendment v4 (2026-10-29, before v4 probing; responds to sol-high review v1, score 68)

# sgen011 DRAFT design — fresh patient-level evaluation (NOT locked)

Status: lead-drafted 2026-10-29 while model-call allocations
(phase2_lock1/phase6_7) are exhausted. This is design prep only. The
generation itself must still be generated by sol-xhigh and ledger-locked
before any outcome access, per campaign rules. Nothing here authorizes
downloading or opening outcome files.

## Established pool composition (lead-computed from pinned sgen010 inputs)
- 1,106 established models / 1,069 confirmed SIDP patients / 1,068 DepMap PatientIDs
- Lineage: 30 Oncotree lineages (Lung 120, Lymphoid 91, CNS/Brain 86, ...)
- Growth: Adherent 847, Suspension 156, Mixed 53, Unknown 39, Dome 11
- Type: Cell Line 1,095, Organoid 11 (the 11 are HCM-SANG-* models resolved
  via HCMI/SIDM; 97 screened organoids remain identity-unresolved)
- Media: 129 distinct OnboardedMedia formulations; serum-free only 12
- Within-patient replication: 35 patients with >=2 established models (max 4)

## Design tension to resolve at generation time
The locked Lock-S estimand concerned organoid rank displacement joined to
paired-format lability. The established pool is overwhelmingly adherent cell
lines; only 11 established organoids exist. A fresh evaluation therefore
cannot simply re-run the Lock-S estimand on this pool. Candidate framings
for sol-xhigh to adjudicate (none selected here):
A. Patient-level replication of the lability/displacement DIRECTION on cell
   lines grouped by measured culture environment (growth pattern / media
   formulation strata), with patient as the resampling unit - tests transport
   of the mechanism beyond organoids; estimand differs from Lock-S and must
   be pre-registered as new, not a re-test of C.
B. Organoid-restricted design conditional on resolving the 97 unresolved
   organoids' identities (requires an identity resource beyond the two
   supplied files - e.g. Passports API receipts like pgen003, or user-supplied
   crosswalk); power at ~100 organoid patients needs assessment.
C. Two-stage: (i) metadata-only power/identifiability generation comparing A
   and B on measurable strata; (ii) locked outcome generation only for the
   surviving framing.

## Inputs a future locked generation would need (not yet requested)
- DepMap 26Q3 CRISPR outcome matrix for established models ONLY after lock
  (user portal download; hash-pinned at acquisition like sgen010 inputs).
- For framing B: an authoritative organoid identity crosswalk.
- Model-call allocation (sol-xhigh generation + sol-high reviews) - currently
  exhausted; needs user budget amendment.
- C8/C9 policy track remains separately blocked on metered host-cost witness.

## Hard constraints carried forward
- Cohort C never reused; patient is the inference unit; no endpoint switch
  after lock; single execution under commit (Lock-S pattern); outcomes for
  unresolved/name-only models stay untouched unless identity resolves first.

- **Generator-protocol freeze (isolates policy improvement):** for any policy comparison, the *entire* generation protocol is frozen and versioned — proposer prompt, direction-summary prompt, catalog-extraction prompt+schema, candidate ranking inputs, repair/unstick allowances, model IDs + efforts. Fixed arms run the **same protocol on their own admissible histories**. Any discretionary intervention outside the frozen protocol is logged as a **protocol breach**. The primary comparison is **assignment-retentive**: all assigned attempts, failures, and costs stay in their arm (no post-hoc exclusion of inconvenient outcomes). Exclusions are allowed **only** under predeclared, outcome-independent criteria frozen before the comparison. A breach that changes admissible information or treatment **invalidates the affected comparison** (restart requires appropriately unused evaluation evidence); logging/charging the breach never repairs biased inclusion. Only the executable **policy module** differs between arms.
- **Context/retrieval contract:** "exhaustive/full history" always means **exhaustive over the episode's admissible history** (§0.4.2 filter) — the same filter applies to *every* input channel: history index, retrieved records, rendered prompts, summaries, priorities, and unstick packets. Proposer inputs (token-bounded by construction; budgets frozen in the SPEC with reserved space for instructions + retrieved records): (a) **bounded directory header** — partition list with counts and ID ranges only (never a full ID dump), (b) **history index partitions** (fixed-size rows: ID, direction, origin, parents, outcome class, quality, cost), partitioned deterministically by direction and **sub-partitioned by fixed row/token caps so no partition — including one huge direction — exceeds its bound**, (c) episode-admissible catalog/frontier view, (d) direction summary, (e) full records via a **runner-mediated ID lookup** (proposer cites IDs or ID ranges; runner resolves partition→records deterministically, budgeted per generation, every lookup logged; cross-partition access always by ID). Complete addressability = every admissible ID is reachable via header→partition→lookup, without ever rendering the whole directory. **Overflow outcome:** if no legal rendering fits the frozen token budget, the generation call splits further (finer sub-partitions, header unchanged) — if still infeasible, the SPEC must narrow its index scope explicitly and the narrowing is ledgered; silent truncation is forbidden. Fixtures required: directory-alone-exceeds-cap and single-direction-exceeds-cap cases both rendering legally. What each call received is recorded in its input manifest. This is the single definition of "full tried history" used in GOAL.md. The hidden-outcome invariance test (§0.4.2) must cover the **complete rendered input and resulting decisions**, all channels included.

### 0.4 Trajectory system (Dream-RSI adaptation — departures disclosed)

Adapted from Dream-RSI (arXiv:2609.14858; `google-research/dream-rsi`): discovery history as replay simulator; offline policy improvement ("dreaming") then online redeployment; fixed generator+evaluator+task, only policy changes. Spec constraints override the paper where they conflict; then the method is labeled **Dream-RSI-inspired adaptation**.

**0.4.1 Units & DAG schema.** *Node/attempt* = one evaluated artifact. Every node has an **ordered parent array** (possibly empty, one, or many), forming an **acyclic** lineage DAG validated at insert. Each parent edge records the parent's immutable contribution (which components carried over). Nodes carry `study_id`, `evaluator_version`, `world_id` (the round/tree that produced them; recombination children belong to their birth world and reference parents across worlds by ID). **Replay eligibility:** a node is replayable in an episode only if (a) every information-bearing parent is either revealed earlier in the episode or in the initially-available set, (b) study/evaluator versions match the episode, and (c) its canonical input manifest matches the episode state (§0.4.6). **Ancestry cost** = cost of the union of required ancestor nodes, charged **once** per episode (Phase 5 allocation). *Branch/trajectory* = the primary-parent (first-parent) chain view of the DAG, used for best-so-far curves; *discovery tree* = one round's forest under one policy on one panel, frozen+hashed into the **trace pool** as a replay world (pool only grows). Tree shape `BRANCHES × (REFINE+1)` scaled to budget; exact values frozen at Lock 1. *Direction* = coherent research line over many nodes.

*Identities (dedup done right, arm-scoped):* `attempt_id` · `context_hash` · `config_id` · `evaluation_id` (config × data × split × evaluator version). **Duplicate eligibility is computed only against the acting arm's episode-admissible history**, scoped by (study, panel, split): the same `config_id` under a new `evaluation_id` (genuinely new evidence/panel) is legal under the frozen symmetric-evaluation rule; re-running an existing `evaluation_id` *within the same arm scope* is a replication (prespecified reason required). The global artifact store retains bytes for audit, but **global membership never changes any arm's observations, rejections, or legal actions** (no existence-oracle across arms/episodes). Required tests: adding hidden/other-arm configs must not change an arm's behavior; reversing arm execution order must not change either arm's outcomes. Trial accounting uses these levels (§0.5.1.8).

**0.4.2 Direction catalog with episode views.** `directions/catalog.json` + immutable snapshots (`history/iterNNN.json`). Status is **four independent fields**, each with deterministic predicates in a **total transition table frozen at Lock 1** (every state combination + missing-evidence + precedence + recovery transitions defined; each transition cites evidence node IDs): `depth` ∈ {unexplored, underexplored, explored, well_explored} · `promise` ∈ {unknown, unpromising, promising} · `fragility` ∈ {unknown, robust, fragile} · `recoverability` ∈ {n/a, recoverable, dead}. Derived labels (e.g. "saturated" = depth well_explored + marginal-gain < ε over last k attempts) are **resource-allocation judgments, never scientific exhaustion verdicts**. Catalog also stores: evidence attempt IDs, best/median quality, quality-vs-cost slope, failure taxonomy, `avoid_repeating`, bottlenecks. Extraction (sol-xhigh, schema-validated) proposes classifications; **deterministic predicates verify them** against recorded outcomes — mismatches rejected+ledgered.
**Episode views (no future leakage):** anything fed to a policy/generator during replay — catalog snapshot, frontier, summaries, priorities, legal actions — is **recomputed from admissible history only**: complete earlier worlds + the revealed prefix of the current world. Global/current catalog objects never enter replay. Acceptance test: mutating any unrevealed outcome must not change any episode-view artifact or policy decision (hidden-outcome invariance test).

**0.4.3 Trajectory scoring (formal, deterministic, no LLM).** Locked at Lock 1 with formulas; defaults: per-node **valid quality** `q ∈ [0,1]` = locked monotone transform of the primary scientific endpoint (higher = better; sign/direction fixed in contract; invalid ⇒ no q, counted invalid, never 0-as-quality). Per trajectory with cumulative measured cost `c`: best-valid-so-far `B(c) = max q over valid nodes with cumulative cost ≤ c` (0 if none); **cost-to-threshold** `C(τ) = min c with B(c) ≥ τ`, else **censored at budget** (never an invented number); **normalized area-over-curve** `AoC = (1/B_ep) ∫₀^{B_ep} B(c) dc` over the episode budget `B_ep`; validity rate; **robustness** `R` = locked sensitivity statistic (e.g. min quality retained across prespecified sensitivity replicates, formula at Lock 1). **Pareto frontier** computed **within a comparable domain** (same task panel + evaluator version + endpoint) over (final B, total cost, R). Precedence: frontier membership = evidence quality; saturation/pruning = allocation status — a nondominated-but-saturated trajectory stays frontier-listed but allocation-paused; neither label overwrites the other.

**0.4.4 Origins & generation.** Sol-xhigh proposes candidates under the frozen protocol (§0.1); each declares exactly one node-operation/origin:
- `new` (0 parents; opens unexplored direction) · `refinement` (exactly 1 parent; mutate/extend a frontier or winner artifact) · `underexplored_extension` (1+ parents in a thin-evidence direction) · `combination` (≥2 parents; each contribution stated; legality of each element checked; revalidated from scratch; no score inheritance) · `repair` (≥1 parent + cited failure node ID + named fix).
Runner rejects (ledgered, fed back next round): outside locked spaces; duplicate `config_id` without replication authorization; nonexistent parents/evidence; `avoid_repeating` repeats without `repair` justification; cyclic or version-incompatible lineage.

**0.4.5 Selection = executable policy over prefix-recomputed state.** Proposal (sol-xhigh: what *could* run + priorities as inputs) ≠ selection (versioned `policy(episode_view, legal_actions, remaining_budget) → action`). **Legal actions are recomputed at each step from the revealed prefix** using frozen transition/pruning rules — historical legal-action sequences are audit records, never counterfactual state for challengers. Keep/prune: frontier trajectories refinable; allocation-paused (saturated) directions leave the legal set until a frozen reactivation rule fires; `fragile` trajectories refinable only via prespecified robustness diagnostics. Deterministic recomputation covers all code-computed state. **LLM-produced state** (direction summaries, rankings, proposals, extraction text) is **immutable memoized output**: stored content-addressed, keyed by (canonical admissible-state hash, generator-protocol version); replay/offline reconstruction **reads the memo — never re-invokes the model**. Cache miss during replay ⇒ that transition is `unsupported` (online execution may create the memo, charged once at creation, then reused). Required test: repeated reconstruction from the same revealed outcomes yields byte-identical rendered inputs with zero additional model calls. Catalog *classifications* remain predicate-verified deterministically (§0.4.2); free-text summaries/rankings are memo-replayed, not regenerated.

**0.4.6 Dreaming: replay objective, ρ, exact context, common support.**
- **ρ is a budget-control parameter** (as in the paper): replay evaluates each policy at operating budgets `ρ·B_ep` for ρ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}. **Replay objective (complete formula frozen at Lock 1; default):** per episode e and ρ, `J_e(π,ρ) = B_e(ρ·B_ep)` (best valid quality attained within that budget; invalid nodes contribute cost, no quality; zero-attainment ⇒ 0). Policy score `J(π) = Σ_ρ w_ρ · mean_e J_e(π,ρ)` over the **common eligible episode set** (below) with locked weights `w_ρ` (default uniform). **Total ordering (frozen before replay; no residual ties):** (1) higher J; (2) higher attainment fraction `P(B_e(B_ep) ≥ τ)`; (3) lower **restricted-mean cost-to-τ** `mean_e min(C_e(τ), B_ep)` (identifiable under censoring); (4) earlier position in the SPEC's pre-listed candidate order; (5) lexicographically smaller immutable candidate ID. The incumbent participates as an ordinary candidate in this ordering; "retain incumbent" is simply the outcome when the incumbent orders first — never an extra discretionary step. Costs are measured ledger costs (§0.4.1 ancestry rule); endpoints' signs/scales per contract.
- **Exact context (operational; history-dependent, not "parent-local"):** refinement generation is **history-dependent exact-context replay** — the generator's inputs are exactly its canonical manifest (parent artifact(s) + frozen instruction + episode-view snapshot ID + budget token + retrieved records). A recorded child replays **iff** the challenger's episode state reproduces that manifest hash exactly; **any differing input ⇒ `unsupported`**, never approximated. Before any screening reliance, Phase 3/4 must **measure attainable support on reordered traces** (including context-overflow and budget-token variation) and report it; if attainable support fails §below thresholds, replay screening is inadmissible by construction for that comparison.
- **Common support (frozen at Lock 1; no policy-specific deletion):** for each ρ separately, an episode is **fully supported for policy π at ρ** if every decision π requests within budget `ρ·B_ep` replays as supported. The **common eligible set at ρ** = episodes fully supported for **every** compared policy at that ρ (intersection; fixed episode-level denominator = the frozen episode list size, never trajectory-length-dependent). `J_e` means are computed **only on the common eligible set, identically for all policies** — policies are never ranked on different surviving sets. **Adequacy:** if the common set at any ρ with `w_ρ > 0` falls below the locked threshold (default ≥ 8 episodes **and** ≥ 50% of the frozen list), the screen is **inadmissible** for that comparison → fresh rollouts decide (§Phase 4 fallback). Unsupported actions terminate that policy's episode copy as `unsupported` (removing the episode from the common set for everyone at that ρ, reported per-policy as the cause) and can **never** count as cheap successful stops. Coverage (per policy, per ρ) always reported beside scores.
- Both arms share the same first round **E0** (starting policy; copied read-only; its production cost charged per Phase 5 allocation — copying is not free).

**0.4.7 Audit views.** `status --trajectories`: lineage DAG (all parents), direction board (4-field statuses), frontier data, generation-over-generation table, allocation-paused list + reasons, coverage reports. Derived deterministically from ledgers; ledger wins on disagreement (= view bug).

### 0.5 Generation protocol (adapted from the business LOOP, hardened)

Modeled on `~/bufferright/business/data/research/paths/LOOP/` (48 generations; "Sol xhigh proposes, Sol high reviews"; score trails 54→76→92). Translation: sleeve pool → analysis-family pool; blend → `combination`; PREREG hash → SPEC hash; forward ledger → frozen predictions; anchor → evaluator-compatibility suite (below). **Two separate lifecycles** (never mixed): **(S) scientific-artifact generations** and **(P) policy generations**, each with own SPEC, screen, battery, denominators, trial counters.

**0.5.1 Anatomy (`generations/{s,p}genNNN/`, never reused/overwritten).**
1. **SPEC.md + SHA-256 locked in ledger before any run:** discriminating question, candidate families, screen definition (incl. whether it is a *necessary-condition* screen — §0.5.2), battery definition, pass bar, stop rules, reserved battery budget. Amendments = new versioned files; locked-science amendments follow new-study-ID rule.
2. **Enumerate** from the pool under frozen protocol; origins+parents per §0.4.4; legality validated.
3. **Screen (ranking only, labeled approximate).** Screen-positives are never claims.
4. **Recombine/refine winners** (`combination`/`refinement`); re-enter at screen; no score inheritance.
5. **Battery (decisive):** (S) full frozen evaluator + validity + matched controls + ablations on fresh development rollouts; (P) Phase 4/5 procedure (replay screen → fresh paired rollouts incl. incumbent). Battery budget is **reserved before screening**; if ceilings intervene, unfinished batteries are `PENDING`, never silently dropped.
6. **Verdicts are scoped to what was tested:** `ADVANCES` · `FAILS-BATTERY (tested finalists: n/N, with numbers)` · `FAMILY-CLOSED` (allowed **only** with a proven necessary-condition screen or exhaustive battery — §0.5.2; else untested members remain explicitly open) · `INVALID` (defective record preserved, corrected in a new version) · `BLOCKED-DATA` (no proxy substitution without claim downgrade) · `PENDING`.
7. **Sol-high review → verify → fix → re-review to ≥ 90**, per-issue dispositions (`CONFIRMED+FIXED` / `ACCEPTED with claim downgrade` / `REJECTED with evidence`).
8. **`GENERATIONS.md` entry:** numbers for every finalist incl. failures, lessons, next mandate, stop-rule checks (leakage ⇒ dependent lines cancelled), and **multi-counter trial accounting** (cumulative, separate: unique configs, attempts, replications, hypothesis inspections, policy candidates, replay episodes, batteries — scientific vs engineering adaptation never merged into one total; no count substitutes for confirmatory procedure).

**0.5.2 Screening honesty.** A screen justifies exhaustive rejection **only** if passing it is a mathematically necessary condition for passing the battery (proof stated in SPEC, e.g. battery metric is a monotone refinement bounded by the screen metric). Otherwise verdicts read "no *tested finalist* passes" and screen-negative members stay listed as untested. Cheapest-falsification probes run as one fixed SPEC with no variants; failure closes only the tested specification, with family-level closure requiring the necessary-condition argument.

**0.5.3 Evaluator versioning (anchor is not certification).** Scores from different evaluator versions are **never pooled** in one comparison/replay pool. The frozen baseline "anchor" reproduction is a smoke check only. Any evaluator change requires: compatibility suite (rankings + validity decisions on a frozen probe set), explicit invalidation list for affected results, and — if substantive — the new-study/new-evidence procedure. Versions preserved side-by-side.

**0.5.4 Matched controls & post-hoc rule.** A new ingredient is credited only vs a same-construction control lacking it; unmatched construction changes are disclosed as non-decomposable. Post-hoc discoveries (e.g. control beats hypothesis) are flagged post-hoc, may be frozen for forward judging, never promotable on consumed data.

**0.5.5 Generation boundary (end-to-end).** Deterministic scores/frontier/episode views → sol-xhigh direction summary + ranked proposal (keep / recombine-with-rationale / repair / open / pause, all ID-cited) → policy code executes selection under budget → runs → extraction + predicate verification → sol-high ≥ 90 → ledger + trace-pool append.

### 0.6 Autonomy, unstick protocol, campaign limits & terminal determination
- **Default = continue autonomously** through failures/negative results, generation after generation, **within campaign allocations** (Lock 1: per-phase + total wall/nodes/model-calls, inside §0.2 ceilings). Legitimate stops: hard authorization gate (credential/spending/required file), allocation/ceiling exhaustion, explicit user stop, no-progress determination (below), terminal determination.
- **Unstick (sol-xhigh):** on stall (no obvious legal action, unexpected gate failure, all directions paused/dead/blocked, contradictory results, same failure twice) invoke sol-xhigh with the state packet (STATUS, episode views, frontier, last 3 generation entries, blocker + attempts) for ranked unblocks + cheapest discriminating experiment + draft next SPEC. Verify vs locked contract (sol cannot authorize contract/ceiling/final-access/standard changes); ledger consultation+disposition; **unstick calls are charged costs** (Phase 5). Max 3 consultation rounds per blocker, then smallest legal evidence-gathering action. Under a frozen comparison, unstick input is restricted to that arm's admissible history (§0.1 freeze).
- **No-progress / negative-EV rule (prevents indefinite retries, spec §14):** applies **before Lock 1 too**, against §0.2 pre-lock allocations: a pre-lock blocker (crosswalk, pairing, review gate) surviving its repeat-failure limit, or K consecutive generations (K default 3, finalized at Lock 1) with no frontier movement / new identifiable question / gate progress, triggers joint sol-xhigh + lead assessment; concurrence ⇒ admissible **non-complete terminal determination** (`INCONCLUSIVE`/`BLOCKED`) with unmet gates + smallest next step. Gate reviews exceeding the Phase-0 round cap escalate to the user with the residual issue list rather than looping.
- **Terminal determination (sol-xhigh judges, evidence rules):** `COMPLETE_*` requires sol-xhigh's written gate-by-gate (C1–C13) certification over the full evidence package, score ≥ 90, zero unresolved high/critical — **in addition to** the evidence, never instead of it; it cannot waive gates. A **pre-reserved terminal-review budget slice** (Lock 1) guarantees the call is affordable; if it still cannot run, the executor may mechanically checkpoint and report `BLOCKED`/`BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` honestly — but **positive completion always requires the sol-xhigh determination**. Non-complete determinations list exact unmet gates; consumed Layer-B/C evidence stays consumed (Phases 5–6).

## Phase 2 — Vertical slice, baselines, Lock 1 (Gate G2 → C4–C5)
1. **Estimators (Layer-A only):** paired within-model contrasts in original units — both conditions, **all individual paired changes**, uncertainty, heterogeneity. **Joint uncertainty is mandatory with the correct independent unit:** the resampling unit is selected from the crosswalk — **donors** (resampling a donor carries *all* its nested models, cultures, contrasts, and every gene's paired vector together) whenever multiple models share a donor; models only when donor≡model is verified. Uncertain donor identity ⇒ conservative grouping (possibly-shared treated as shared) **plus** a sensitivity analysis under the split assumption; both reported. An explicit covariance model may substitute only with justification. Downstream transfer analyses refit per replicate; conclusions that flip are reported. Per-gene independent error bars alone are non-conforming. Effective sample sizes (donors *and* models) reported; few clusters ⇒ justify or downgrade intervals/tests. Tests include nested-donor fixtures.
2. **Baselines** (same rows/info; preprocessing/selection/tuning inside development folds only): lineage-only; genotype-only; state/expression-only; genotype+state; +context/assay; regularized-linear à la S3 (from Zenodo code where possible). Final-outcome reproductions deferred to post-Lock-2. **Fold construction matches the generalization claim (blocked evaluation, spec §9):** fold manifests are frozen artifacts; for unseen-donor prediction, **every conservatively-linked donor's models, cultures, and repeated observations sit in exactly one fold — including nested tuning folds** (donor-grouped CV, same conservative grouping as §Phase 2.1); lineage/target/pathway blocking added where the claim requires it. Invalid rules: leakage, support violations, and **verified orientation/preprocessing errors** ⇒ `invalid`. **The main feasibility risk is now shared processing cost**

Let \(S\) be shared CPU production cost, \(H\) learned-system overhead, and \(L,F\) learned and strongest-fixed deployment CPU over **one actual reserved campaign**. Twenty-percent end-to-end savings requires

\[
S+H+L\le0.8(S+F),
\qquad
F\ge0.25S+1.25(H+L).

Raw normalization, reference construction and shared pilot production belong in \(S\), even if performed before rollout. All learning and review dependencies belong in the end-to-end accounting.

# OpenAI Docs

Provide current, cited OpenAI product, API, model, and Codex guidance. Read zero or one primary reference.

**First substantive action:** Search the user's exact requested official OpenAI documentation topic and any explicitly named model using a concise, topic-specific query of 2-6 essential terms. When an already-available direct official documentation search and page-retrieval capability is present, use it first: search, then fetch or open the matching official page before general web search. Otherwise, immediately use official-domain web search, then actually open or fetch the relevant official page. Complete this source order before reading a reference, inspecting local or repository files, running a Codex manual or model resolver, drafting a plan, or answering from memory. Use the actual fetched page, not a search snippet or an unopened link. If one official search or page does not establish the answer, search another appropriate official domain and actually open or fetch the result. Preserve the exact requested model; never substitute a newer model.

**Only exception:** An explicitly requested, genuinely broad, cross-topic Codex setup, orientation, or system-map synthesis may use the manual first when shell execution and an allowed temporary cache are available. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

For generic software tasks, answer the software task directly. OpenAI implementation, debugging, SDK, API, prompting, agent, and eval requests are not generic.

For a straightforward factual or citation-only request, follow the source order and do not read a route reference. This includes straightforward API facts, ChatGPT Work or mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons, model tiers, aliases, Pro mode, reasoning settings, factual migration baselines, and narrow Codex facts. Prioritize `learn.chatgpt.com` for ChatGPT Work.

## Choose one primary route

Use the first matching route, and read its reference only when the requested task needs that specialized workflow:

- **Explicitly requested local documentation integration:** Read [integration guidance](references/mcp-diagnostics.md) only when the user explicitly requests that local integration.
- **Model migration, upgrades, or model-specific prompting:** Read [model-migration.md](references/model-migration.md) for actual migration planning, implementation, dynamic target resolution, or prompt changes. Preserve an explicitly requested target.
- **Model selection and comparisons:** Read [model-selection.md](references/model-selection.md) only when nuanced current, latest, default, cost, latency, quality, or modality tradeoffs need more guidance. Do not run a migration resolver for selection alone.
- **Product, API, ChatGPT Work, and mixed Chat/Work/Codex documentation:** Read [official-docs.md](references/official-docs.md) only when fetched official pages leave source selection, API schemas, or the requested implementation unresolved. This route is not manual-first.
- **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

Read at most one primary reference. Do not open every route, bundled model guide, or helper script. Read a supporting reference or run a helper only when the chosen workflow demonstrably needs it.

## Source and execution boundaries

- Search, open, fetch, and cite only `developers.openai.com`, `platform.openai.com`, and `learn.chatgpt.com`. Cite the page that supports the claim. State uncertainty when official sources do not establish pricing, availability, account access, limits, or behavior.
- Preserve an explicitly requested model for selection, migration, and prompting. Resolve an unspecified latest or current migration target only after searching and fetching current official guidance.
- Use `references/latest-model.md` only as a disclosed fallback after current official model guidance does not answer the question. Read `references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md` only for an actual, requested GPT-6 migration; read `references/prompting-guide.md` only for requested prompting work.
- Before building, running, editing, debugging, or testing an API-backed app or tool, use `openai-platform-api-key` first when available. Documentation, conceptual examples, model selection, and read-only guidance do not require an API key.
- Say "OpenAI Docs" or "official OpenAI documentation" in user-facing answers. Keep exact official citations and examples concise.

Create `cancer-dependency-rsi/` (README, GOAL copy+hash, PROTOCOL stub, STATUS+status.json, `config/{resources,host}.json`, `src/`, `data/`, `ledger/`, `reviews/`, `artifacts/`, `generations/`, `directions/`, `trace_pool/`, `tests/`, `manuscript/`); project `.venv` via uv + lockfile; implement first: budget wrapper (§0.2 tests incl. concurrency/retries/interruption), append-only ledgers, artifact store, hashing, CLI skeleton (`bootstrap, audit-data, reproduce-baselines, run-pilot, run-cycle, evaluate-policy, lock-science, evaluate-external, reproduce, status, resume` — gate-locked commands fail loudly naming the gate). Record host fingerprint without secrets. **G0:** status/resume work; dummy over-budget job demonstrably killed (timeout+RSS); tests green; sol-high ≥ 90. *(Status 2026-10-28: scaffold + ledger/budget + 3 tests done; CLI + remaining tests pending.)*

## Phase 1 — Quarantine-first verification & identifiability audit (Gate G1 → C1–C3)
**1a. Metadata-only first.** Before importing any outcome-bearing file: create **provisional A/B/C partitions from metadata alone** (model/donor/lineage lists, no outcome values), write the **quarantine + exposure log** (every outcome-file access records who/what/when/which partition). Permitted pre-Lock-1 outcome contact: **Layer-A (development) sources only** (incl. the Broad minipool + genome-wide development data) and *published* QC summaries for B/C candidates. Sanger outcome matrices, once imported, sit quarantined as Layer-C candidates: schema/shape/control-gene inventory checks allowed via logged scripts; **no outcome-value inspection, ranking, or modeling** until Lock 2. Any accidental exposure is logged and downgrades affected claims.
**1b. Read primary sources in full** (S1 PMC13581591, S2 PMC13581617, S3 PMC13664187 + Zenodo 22472622, S5 arXiv:2609.14858 + repo): exact designs, selection rules, score definitions/directions, QC, published findings (= controls). *(Done at full-text level 2026-10-28; supplements/code deep-read continues.)*
**1c. Routes via official manifests only** — source URL, release/commit, date, license, bytes, SHA-256 per file into `data/source_manifest*.json`. Never invent URLs; never bypass challenges (DepMap portal verification page ⇒ use study-specific figshare releases, preferred anyway). **Leakage rule (spec §5, corrected):** if any correction/normalization/**target or model selection** used external outcomes, that evidence requires **development-only reconstruction or genuinely independent validation — disclosure never repairs it**; otherwise the independence gate stays **unmet**. Only **covariate-only** joint preprocessing may proceed as disclosed transductive preprocessing with limited claims. Audit Chronos pre-training + 26Q3 integration under this rule.
**1d. Provenance + crosswalk + counts:** model/donor/lineage/origin/lab/library/medium/format/replicate/release/outcome; Broad↔HCMI↔Sanger↔author IDs; uncertain donor = `uncertain`; count **independent models/donors** (genes/guides/wells/cultures ≠ patients); attrition registry. Verify seeds at row level. *(Minipool verified: 7 models, 18 screens, 5 medium + 7 format matched contrasts, 250 selected genes, 0 missing; ACH-003052 lineage gap + HCM-SANG↔ACH crosswalk open.)*
**1e. Assay audit (Layer-A + published summaries):** Chronos vs Sanger LFC/BAGEL — direction, range, controls, missingness, QC per source; absolute values never interchanged/subtracted. Confirm required pairings exist before modeling; check lab↔biology confounding.
**1f. Novelty audit v1:** dated search (queries/exclusions preserved) + claim ledger (nearest prior, established part, precise residual uncertainty, evidence needed, consequences). Rule out generic 2D→organoid transfer (S3) and published format/medium class findings (S1) as novelty.
**Gate G1:** named falsifiable question in a named subset + counted independent units + documented paired contrasts (or documented narrower question; broader component recorded unmet). No adaptive search before G1. Sol-high ≥ 90 on provenance + novelty package.

## Phase 2 — Vertical slice, baselines, Lock 1 (Gate G2 → C4–C5)
1. **Estimators (Layer-A only):** paired within-model contrasts in original units — both conditions, **all individual paired changes**, uncertainty, heterogeneity. **Joint uncertainty is mandatory with the correct independent unit:** the resampling unit is selected from the crosswalk — **donors** (resampling a donor carries *all* its nested models, cultures, contrasts, and every gene's paired vector together) whenever multiple models share a donor; models only when donor≡model is verified. Uncertain donor identity ⇒ conservative grouping (possibly-shared treated as shared) **plus** a sensitivity analysis under the split assumption; both reported. An explicit covariance model may substitute only with justification. Downstream transfer analyses refit per replicate; conclusions that flip are reported. Per-gene independent error bars alone are non-conforming. Effective sample sizes (donors *and* models) reported; few clusters ⇒ justify or downgrade intervals/tests. Tests include nested-donor fixtures.
2. **Baselines** (same rows/info; preprocessing/selection/tuning inside development folds only): lineage-only; genotype-only; state/expression-only; genotype+state; +context/assay; regularized-linear à la S3 (from Zenodo code where possible). Compare vs **strongest**; prespecified environmental ablation; matched controls for any new ingredient. Final-outcome reproductions deferred to post-Lock-2. **Fold construction matches the generalization claim (blocked evaluation, spec §9):** fold manifests are frozen artifacts; for unseen-donor prediction, **every conservatively-linked donor's models, cultures, and repeated observations sit in exactly one fold — including nested tuning folds** (donor-grouped CV, same conservative grouping as §Phase 2.1); lineage/target/pathway blocking added where the claim requires it. Row-level random folds are non-conforming for donor-generalization claims. (Within-model paired environmental contrasts are a separate design, not CV folds, and remain governed by §Phase 2.1.) Required fixture: distinct model IDs sharing one donor must never straddle folds — build fails otherwise.
3. **Evaluator v1** (separate module, narrow interface): effect sizes + calibrated predictive/uncertainty endpoints; **never** p-value size / discovery count / narrative confidence. Invalid rules: leakage, support violations, and **verified orientation/preprocessing errors** ⇒ `invalid`. A correctly measured **opposite-direction result is valid evidence** (potential refutation/heterogeneity), never invalidated for direction alone.
4. **Lock 1 — freeze contract** (`PROTOCOL.md` + `contract.json`, hashed with evaluator + splits + generator protocol). Mandatory fields: question + falsifiable alternatives; population/environments/targets/generalization; eligibility; data/ID versions; **final A/B/C partitions** (blocked, overlap-recorded, refining Phase-1a provisionals using metadata only); feature/transform rules; endpoints (primary/secondary, fixed direction, q-transform §0.4.3); **meaningful-dependency-strength requirement for every positive vulnerability claim** (predeclared threshold in each claimed environment, tested independently of the environmental-change criterion; stable non-dependency ≠ vulnerability); practical-effect/equivalence margins + justification (no margin ⇒ no "invariant" label); multiplicity (default Holm FWER 0.05, small family) + joint-uncertainty method; baselines; invalid rules; success/failure/inconclusive/exhaustion; **trajectory machinery** (BRANCHES/REFINE, status transition table, replay objective + ρ weights, support thresholds, episode sets); **policy-comparison design** (Phase 5: resource endpoint fully specified, # independent blocks, savings estimand, paired estimator, censoring-compatible CI, precision-feasibility result, cost-allocation rules); **campaign allocations + retry/no-progress limits + terminal-review reserve**; context/retrieval contract. Change ⇒ new study ID + new evidence.
5. **Tests:** leakage (donor overlap A/B/C fails build), score direction, grouping, synthetic-estimator behavior (code only), cost/reservation suite, resume idempotence, unsupported-replay, **hidden-outcome invariance** (§0.4.2), DAG acyclicity/version compat, final-outcome access guard + exposure log, evaluator-compatibility probe set.
**Gate G2:** baselines reproduced on Layer-A (direction/cohort/measurement integrity; discrepancies bounded in writing); all hashes committed. Sol-high ≥ 90. **No policy optimization before G2.** *(Precursor measured: paired-mean vs published coefficients r = 0.91 format / 0.96 medium on test250.)*

## Phase 3 — Pilot E0 + Replay World v1 (Gate G3, interim)
Run the hand-designed **fixed exploration policy** (executable module; legal actions: open family / refine / diagnostic / stop; never labels/splits/metrics/margins) on Layer-A tasks to **24 evaluated nodes** under the frozen generator protocol. Freeze trees as **E0 / Replay World v1** + support-coverage report. **G3 issues an interim pilot report only** (verified data, identifiable question, baselines, real nodes, replay support, measured costs, next discriminating experiment) with policy comparison explicitly **unperformed** — G3 does **not** establish C13. Sol-high ≥ 90.

## Phase 4 — Policy-improvement cycles (Gate G4 → C8, C13)
Per cycle (≥ 2 genuine cycles; retained incumbent is valid), executed as (P)-generations (§0.5):
1. Generate **incumbent + ≥ 3 executable challengers** (sol-xhigh code rewrites under frozen protocol; reflections without changed decisions don't count).
2. **Replay-screen** all on identical frozen episode sets (§0.4.6 rules). **Selection/fallback is pre-registered in the (P)-SPEC before replay runs:** if the screen is admissible → fresh-test the top-1 challenger by J (ties per §0.4.6); if inadmissible → fresh-test challengers in the SPEC's pre-listed order (recorded before any replay output exists) until the cycle's frozen fresh-rollout allocation is spent. Every challenger's disposition is ledgered (`FRESH-TESTED` / `NOT-TESTED: screen-rank` / `NOT-TESTED: allocation`) — no discretionary post-hoc picking.
3. **Fresh paired rollouts:** each fresh-tested challenger vs **incumbent** vs fixed exploration (same generator protocol per arm on own histories, evaluator, ceilings, initial artifacts, information; assignment-retentive inclusion §0.1). **Promotion requires beating the incumbent** by the locked improvement/noninferiority rule — beating fixed exploration alone is insufficient; replay superiority never substitutes.
4. Promote or **retain incumbent**; failures kept; append Layer-A histories only; new world version. First completed fresh comparison (or its documented blocker) triggers the **first substantive cycle report** and is the earliest C13 evidence.
**Gate G4:** ≥ 2 cycles ledgered end-to-end (challengers, coverage, paired rollouts, decisions+reasons). Sol-high ≥ 90/cycle. Inadequate replay support ⇒ preserved finding + "Dream-RSI-inspired adaptation" label with departures.

## Phase 5 — Reserved policy evaluation (Gate G5 → C9)
Freeze best admissible policy + selection criterion **before** touching Layer B. Arms: learned vs fixed exploration vs fixed-allocation/random — identical generator protocol (per-arm histories), evaluator version, artifacts, permissions, ceilings; donor/model/gene/pathway-blocked panels (gene splits of the 250 ≠ independent tasks; engineering-cohort → 7-model transfer explicitly bounded).
- **Primary resource endpoint (fully specified at Lock 1):** named resource + units (default USD total measured cost; if an alternative is chosen: justification + its own practical margin + uncertainty criterion + measure-or-strictly-match all other material resources with tolerances); scalarization/aggregation across blocks; quality threshold τ (from development, attainable by baselines); **savings estimand + paired estimator + censoring-compatible interval** (non-attainment = censored, never invented costs); **# independent blocks + precision-feasibility check done at Lock 1** (infeasible precision ⇒ C9 recorded unachievable-by-design before optimization, not discovered after).
- **Ambitious bar (default endpoint):** ≥ 20% savings vs strongest fixed baseline with **one-sided 95% lower bound ≥ 20%** (point > 20% with LB merely > 0 = some improvement, not C9). Report quality-vs-cost curves; end-to-end (incl. learning) and deployment-only views.
- **Cost allocation (frozen, reconciled to resource ledger):** every component charged — generation, evaluation, replay, extraction, summaries, reviews, unstick, failed jobs, promotion trials; E0 + ancestry (§0.4.1) + shared artifacts allocated by the locked rule with stated deployment count (no silent amortization); **information produced in earlier worlds is not free**: each arm is charged the production cost of every history it reads (its own worlds at their recorded costs; shared E0 per the locked split), and both arms receive symmetric *access rules* to earlier-world information (own admissible history only, §0.4.2) — no arm may consume another arm's outcomes at any price. Memoized LLM state (§0.4.5) charged once at creation to its producing arm. Fixed baselines may spend equivalent budget on search. Reported totals must reconcile line-by-line with `ledger/resources.jsonl`.
- **Measurability:** material unmeasurable host-model cost ⇒ C9 `unresolved_cost_gate` (no CPU/token proxy certification). Seeds = execution variability, not biological replication.
- **Consumption:** after evaluation, **B panels are consumed**. Any further adaptation informed by B results (incl. via summaries/reviews) makes later B claims exploratory; a new confirmatory policy claim requires **new independent B evidence**.
**Gate G5:** comparison + uncertainty complete; C9 met / not-met / unresolved with evidence. Sol-high ≥ 90.

## Phase 6 — Lock 2 & single external evaluation (Gate G6 → C6, C10)
1. **Lock 2 (`lock-science`):** exact bounded claim family, predictions, artifacts, inferential code + hashes. **Component-level evidence status attached to every claim** (and later every atlas decision): which dataset validates which component; adaptively reused environmental evidence labeled **exploratory or justified selection-adjusted** (adjustment stated) — external transfer success + Holm never retroactively confirms a selected environmental effect. Claims needing independent environmental confirmation require a suitable independent public controlled-environment dataset, else narrowed or gate-unmet (never gene-splits of the same 7 models). **Causal-interpretation gate (spec §6):** causal/mediation language ("explains *why* transfer fails", mediator claims for expression/state features) requires, per claim, a stated causal estimand + identifying assumptions + evidence suitable under those assumptions; otherwise language is constrained to (i) intervention effects actually measured in the paired environmental panel and (ii) cross-cohort predictive associations — "explanatory finding" in GOAL means this bounded, identified sense, never mechanism-by-association. The gate is applied at Lock 1 (claim templates) and rechecked at Lock 2 + manuscript.
2. **Evaluate once** on Layer C (independently filtered Sanger cohort post-crosswalk/provenance/assay/representation checks; rank/calibration-appropriate cross-study comparisons). Wording: **retrospective** external validation; pretraining/literature exposure recorded.
3. **Prespecified adversarial battery:** locked multiplicity; **dependency-strength gate** (Phase 2) for every positive claim; invariance only with positive dependency + interval-inside-margin equivalence; donor/lineage/platform sensitivity; leave-one-model-out; negative controls; leakage checks; grouping-respecting permutations; environmental ablation; joint-uncertainty fragility report.
**Gate G6:** each claim supported/refuted/inconclusive under frozen rules; failed stays failed. Sol-high adversarial ≥ 90 (tasked to kill claims).

## Phase 7 — Atlas, manuscript, reproduction, determination (Gate G7 → C7, C11–C12)
- **Evidence atlas** (machine-readable): every eligible panel gene — dependency in both conditions, environmental change, uncertainty, heterogeneity, biomarker + transfer evidence, prior knowledge, **component evidence status**, missingness; every exclusion + reason; beyond-panel = exploratory.
- **Manuscript:** estimands, provenance, both locks, baselines, all results incl. failures/retained incumbents, limitations (7 models, selected genes, assay non-interchangeability, retrospective validation, cost measurability), terminal state + unmet gates. No clinical claims from screens. **Dated claim-specific novelty refresh at G7** (and again at terminal determination) — informs C1/C6 currency without revising consumed confirmatory tests.
- **Clean reproduction (`reproduce`):** fresh env from lockfile regenerates estimates/figures/atlas/policy comparison within tolerances from frozen artifacts, **no stochastic LLM rerun** → `reproducibility_report.md`.
- **Terminal determination** per §0.6 (sol-xhigh, gate-by-gate C1–C13). Both `COMPLETE_*` states require all gates incl. C9; else honest state + unmet list.
**Gate G7:** reproduction green; package per §8; sol-high ≥ 90 on manuscript/atlas/report.

**Commands:** `bootstrap → audit-data → reproduce-baselines → run-pilot → run-cycle → evaluate-policy → lock-science → evaluate-external → reproduce` · `status [--trajectories]` · `resume`. Out-of-order execution refused, missing gate named. Every command ledgers its run.

## 9. Reporting
Interim pilot report at G3; **first substantive cycle report** after Phase 4's first fresh comparison (verified data, question, baselines, real experiments, replay support, retained/promoted policy, measured resources incl. `unknown`, next discriminating experiment — or precise blocker + completed independent work). Per-phase: measured results, risks, next experiment. Final: terminal state, C1–C13 evidence table, three status fields, full costs+failures. No progress theater.

## 10. Risks → precommitted responses
| Risk | Response |
|---|---|
| Required pairing unreleased | Stop at G1; narrower documented question; never model the missing contrast |
| 7 models underpower environmental claims | Continuous/heterogeneity estimands; only precision-supported refutations/bounds; seek independent public controlled-environment data or keep gate unmet |
| Donor overlap destroys independence | Crosswalk filtering; downgrade scope/wording; never assume independence |
| Outcome-informed preprocessing (incl. Chronos pretraining/26Q3) | Development-only rebuild or independent validation, else gate unmet; transductive label **only** for covariate-only preprocessing (spec §5) |
| Chronos vs Sanger assay mismatch | Within-study original units; cross-study rank/calibration only |
| Thin replay support | Inadmissible-screen verdict; fresh rollouts decide; adaptation labeled + departures disclosed |
| Host-model costs unmeasurable | C9 `unresolved_cost_gate`; proxies reported separately, never certified |
| Portal/challenge blocks download | Official alternatives (figshare/Europe PMC); documented cache; never bypass |
| Review < 90 stalls | Fix verified only; spec-conflicting demands rejected with citation; genuine conflicts → user |
| Allocation exhausted | Checkpoint; honest terminal state + unmet gates + smallest next step; ceilings never auto-raised |

A reordered branch may alter the context seen by a generator. Make refinement depend on an immutable parent and fixed context, or require an exact context match before replaying a recorded child. Do not assume a recorded child represents an arbitrary counterfactual generation.

The replay policy sees only the outcomes revealed along its trajectory. Do not expose the full tree's future rewards.

Mark unsupported replay actions unsupported. Do not assign them fake scores or treat a surrogate prediction as a measured outcome. Compare policies on common support, report support coverage, and use replay as a screening tool.

Perform the following cycle.

1. Run the initial fixed policy on real development tasks.
2. Preserve the evaluated discovery trees as replay worlds.
3. Generate at least three executable policy challengers plus the unchanged incumbent.
4. Replay them under the same resource constraints and support rules.
5. Select a challenger with the frozen selection rule.
6. Test the challenger in fresh development rollouts against fixed exploration using the same generator and evaluator.
7. Promote only when the preregistered criterion is met.
8. Retain the incumbent when challengers fail.
9. Add only development histories and repeat.

Complete at least two genuine cycles before the final policy comparison if the authorized resources and valid tasks permit. Two cycles do not require two promotions. An unchanged incumbent is a valid experimental outcome.

After development, freeze the best admissible policy and evaluate it on the reserved policy panels. Compare it with the original fixed exploration strategy and at least one simple fixed-allocation or random-selection strategy.


11 - What counts as demonstrated policy improvement

Predeclare one primary operating point or cost-to-quality endpoint. Also report complete scientific-quality-versus-cost curves.

Use the same generator, evaluator, initial artifacts, information permissions, and common resource ceilings for all policies.

Charge policy rewriting, replay, failed jobs, promotion trials, and extra model calls to the improving system. Permit fixed baselines to spend the corresponding budget on scientific search.

Report both end-to-end performance including learning overhead and deployment-only performance with learning costs shown separately.

The ambitious engineering target is at least 20 percent lower total measured API expenditure to reach a predeclared valid scientific-quality threshold, under the same CPU ceiling and information constraints, compared with the strongest fixed baseline. This is a project target, not a forecast.

Set the quality threshold from development evidence before final policy evaluation. It must be meaningful and attainable by competent baselines, not chosen after observing which policy wins.

Use paired blocked comparisons where appropriate and report uncertainty. For the default 20 percent savings goal, require the prespecified one-sided 95 percent lower confidence bound on savings to meet the 20 percent practical margin. A point estimate above 20 percent with a lower bound merely above zero supports some improvement but does not meet that ambitious margin. Freeze how failures to reach the quality threshold within budget are treated as censored outcomes. Do not convert nonattainment into invented exact costs. Random seeds quantify execution variability, not independent biological replication.

If API expenditure is not the dominant or measurable resource, choose a justified alternative primary resource endpoint during the initial contract stage, explain it, and lock it before optimization. All other material resources must still be measured or strictly matched. A CPU-only advantage or token proxy cannot satisfy C9 while material host-model costs remain unknown and unmatched. In that case retain an unresolved cost gate and avoid claiming all-in savings. Define an equally explicit practical improvement margin and uncertainty requirement for any alternative endpoint. Do not switch endpoints after seeing final results.

If faithful replay has inadequate support, preserve that finding and use fresh rollouts to assess the proposed policy. Label the method accurately as a Dream-RSI-inspired adaptation and disclose departures.

Do not call the system recursively self-improving merely because more compute improved a reused validation score.


12 - Completion criteria

Mark the ambitious goal complete only when every applicable criterion below has documentary evidence.

C1 - A current novelty audit identifies a precise unresolved cancer dependency question and distinguishes it from the August resources and October transfer study.

C2 - All analyses use legitimately accessible public data, with complete provenance, licensing, identifier crosswalks, and reproducible retrieval or documented local cache installation.

C3 - The intended paired contrast or conditional relationship is identifiable within a named population. Confounding and selection are disclosed, and independent biological units are counted correctly.

item.aggregated_output:
**Gate G4:** ≥ 2 cycles ledgered end-to-end (challengers, coverage, paired rollouts, decisions+reasons). Sol-high ≥ 90/cycle. Inadequate replay support ⇒ preserved finding + "Dream-RSI-inspired adaptation" label with departures.

## Phase 5 — Reserved policy evaluation (Gate G5 → C9)
Freeze best admissible policy + selection criterion **before** touching Layer B. Arms: learned vs fixed exploration vs fixed-allocation/random — identical generator protocol (per-arm histories), evaluator version, artifacts, permissions, ceilings; donor/model/gene/pathway-blocked panels (gene splits of the 250 ≠ independent tasks; engineering-cohort → 7-model transfer explicitly bounded).
- **Primary resource endpoint (fully specified at Lock 1):** named resource + units (default USD total measured cost; if an alternative is chosen: justification + its own practical margin + uncertainty criterion + measure-or-strictly-match all other material resources with tolerances); scalarization/aggregation across blocks; quality threshold τ (from development, attainable by baselines); **savings estimand + paired estimator + censoring-compatible interval** (non-attainment = censored, never invented costs); **# independent blocks + precision-feasibility check done at Lock 1** (infeasible precision ⇒ C9 recorded unachievable-by-design before optimization, not discovered after).
- **Ambitious bar (default endpoint):** ≥ 20% savings vs strongest fixed baseline with **one-sided 95% lower bound ≥ 20%** (point > 20% with LB merely > 0 = some improvement, not C9). Report quality-vs-cost curves; end-to-end (incl. learning) and deployment-only views.
- **Cost allocation (frozen, reconciled to resource ledger):** every component charged — generation, evaluation, replay, extraction, summaries, reviews, unstick, failed jobs, promotion trials; E0 + ancestry (§0.4.1) + shared artifacts allocated by the locked rule with stated deployment count (no silent amortization); **information produced in earlier worlds is not free**: each arm is charged the production cost of every history it reads (its own worlds at their recorded costs; shared E0 per the locked split), and both arms receive symmetric *access rules* to earlier-world information (own admissible history only, §0.4.2) — no arm may consume another arm's outcomes at any price. Memoized LLM state (§0.4.5) charged once at creation to its producing arm. Fixed baselines may spend equivalent budget on search. Reported totals must reconcile line-by-line with `ledger/resources.jsonl`.
- **Measurability:** material unmeasurable host-model cost ⇒ C9 `unresolved_cost_gate` (no CPU/token proxy certification). Seeds = execution variability, not biological replication.
- **Consumption:** after evaluation, **B panels are consumed**. Any further adaptation informed by B results (incl. via summaries/reviews) makes later B claims exploratory; a new confirmatory policy claim requires **new independent B evidence**.
**Gate G5:** comparison + uncertainty complete; C9 met / not-met / unresolved with evidence. Sol-high ≥ 90.

## Phase 6 — Lock 2 & single external evaluation (Gate G6 → C6, C10)
1. **Lock 2 (`lock-science`):** exact bounded claim family, predictions, artifacts, inferential code + hashes. **Component-level evidence status attached to every claim** (and later every atlas decision): which dataset validates which component; adaptively reused environmental evidence labeled **exploratory or justified selection-adjusted** (adjustment stated) — external transfer success + Holm never retroactively confirms a selected environmental effect. Claims needing independent environmental confirmation require a suitable independent public controlled-environment dataset, else narrowed or gate-unmet (never gene-splits of the same 7 models). **Causal-interpretation gate (spec §6):** causal/mediation language ("explains *why* transfer fails", mediator claims for expression/state features) requires, per claim, a stated causal estimand + identifying assumptions + evidence suitable under those assumptions; otherwise language is constrained to (i) intervention effects actually measured in the paired environmental panel and (ii) cross-cohort predictive associations — "explanatory finding" in GOAL means this bounded, identified sense, never mechanism-by-association. The gate is applied at Lock 1 (claim templates) and rechecked at Lock 2 + manuscript.
2. **Evaluate once** on Layer C (independently filtered Sanger cohort post-crosswalk/provenance/assay/representation checks; rank/calibration-appropriate cross-study comparisons). Wording: **retrospective** external validation; pretraining/literature exposure recorded.
3. **Prespecified adversarial battery:** locked multiplicity; **dependency-strength gate** (Phase 2) for every positive claim; invariance only with positive dependency + interval-inside-margin equivalence; donor/lineage/platform sensitivity; leave-one-model-out; negative controls; leakage checks; grouping-respecting permutations; environmental ablation; joint-uncertainty fragility report.
**Gate G6:** each claim supported/refuted/inconclusive under frozen rules; failed stays failed. Sol-high adversarial ≥ 90 (tasked to kill claims).

## Phase 7 — Atlas, manuscript, reproduction, determination (Gate G7 → C7, C11–C12)
- **Evidence atlas** (machine-readable): every eligible panel gene — dependency in both conditions, environmental change, uncertainty, heterogeneity, biomarker + transfer evidence, prior knowledge, **component evidence status**, missingness; every exclusion + reason; beyond-panel = exploratory.
- **Manuscript:** estimands, provenance, both locks, baselines, all results incl. failures/retained incumbents, limitations (7 models, selected genes, assay non-interchangeability, retrospective validation, cost measurability), terminal state + unmet gates. No clinical claims from screens. **Dated claim-specific novelty refresh at G7** (and again at terminal determination) — informs C1/C6 currency without revising consumed confirmatory tests.
- **Clean reproduction (`reproduce`):** fresh env from lockfile regenerates estimates/figures/atlas/policy comparison within tolerances from frozen artifacts, **no stochastic LLM rerun** → `reproducibility_report.md`.
- **Terminal determination** per §0.6 (sol-xhigh, gate-by-gate C1–C13). Both `COMPLETE_*` states require all gates incl. C9; else honest state + unmet list.
**Gate G7:** reproduction green; package per §8; sol-high ≥ 90 on manuscript/atlas/report.

---

## 8. Artifacts & commands (acceptance inventory)
**Files:** README · GOAL · PROTOCOL+`contract.json` · STATUS+`status.json` · `GENERATIONS.md` · `generations/{s,p}genNNN/{SPEC,screen,battery,reviews}` · `directions/{catalog,history,extraction,summaries}` · `trace_pool/`+manifest · `data/{source_manifest*,model_crosswalk,eligibility_registry,split_manifests,exposure_log}` · `ledger/{claims,experiments,resources,reviews}` · `src/{adapters,baselines,evaluator,policies,replay,runner,budget}` · `artifacts/sha256/` · frozen predictions/models/policies+checksums · `atlas/` · figures · `manuscript/`+limitations+adversarial report · env lock, licenses · `reproducibility_report.md` · `tests/` (§0.2/Phase-2 suites).
**Commands:** `bootstrap → audit-data → reproduce-baselines → run-pilot → run-cycle → evaluate-policy → lock-science → evaluate-external → reproduce` · `status [--trajectories]` · `resume`. Out-of-order execution refused, missing gate named. Every command ledgers its run.

## 9. Reporting
Interim pilot report at G3; **first substantive cycle report** after Phase 4's first fresh comparison (verified data, question, baselines, real experiments, replay support, retained/promoted policy, measured resources incl. `unknown`, next discriminating experiment — or precise blocker + completed independent work). Per-phase: measured results, risks, next experiment. Final: terminal state, C1–C13 evidence table, three status fields, full costs+failures. No progress theater.

## 10. Risks → precommitted responses
| Risk | Response |
|---|---|
| Required pairing unreleased | Stop at G1; narrower documented question; never model the missing contrast |
| 7 models underpower environmental claims | Continuous/heterogeneity estimands; only precision-supported refutations/bounds; seek independent public controlled-environment data or keep gate unmet |
| Donor overlap destroys independence | Crosswalk filtering; downgrade scope/wording; never assume independence |
| Outcome-informed preprocessing (incl. Chronos pretraining/26Q3) | Development-only rebuild or independent validation, else gate unmet; transductive label **only** for covariate-only preprocessing (spec §5) |
| Chronos vs Sanger assay mismatch | Within-study original units; cross-study rank/calibration only |
| Thin replay support | Inadmissible-screen verdict; fresh rollouts decide; adaptation labeled + departures disclosed |
| Host-model costs unmeasurable | C9 `unresolved_cost_gate`; proxies reported separately, never certified |
| Portal/challenge blocks download | Official alternatives (figshare/Europe PMC); documented cache; never bypass |
| Review < 90 stalls | Fix verified only; spec-conflicting demands rejected with citation; genuine conflicts → user |
| Allocation exhausted | Checkpoint; honest terminal state + unmet gates + smallest next step; ceilings never auto-raised |

"""Retained, resumable host/codex calls. No separately metered API is used."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import signal
import subprocess
import time
from budget import reserve, reconcile
from ledger import sha256_file, append_record

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def call_identity(prompt_path,output,effort,phase,terminal,timeout):
    return {'model':'gpt-6.1-sol','effort':effort,'phase':phase,'terminal_review':terminal,
            'timeout_s':timeout,'sandbox':'read-only','interface':'codex exec',
            'binary':os.environ.get('CDRSI_CODEX_BIN','codex'),
            'prompt_sha256':sha256_file(prompt_path),'output':str(output.resolve())}


def call(prompt_path: Path, output: Path, effort: str, phase='phase2_lock1', terminal=False, timeout=600):
    prompt_path = prompt_path.resolve()
    output = output.resolve()
    receipt = output.with_suffix('.receipt.json')
    identity=call_identity(prompt_path,output,effort,phase,terminal,timeout)
    if receipt.exists():
        saved = json.loads(receipt.read_text())
        if saved['prompt_sha256'] != sha256_file(prompt_path):
            raise RuntimeError('immutable call ID reused with different prompt')
        if saved.get('call_identity')!=identity:
            raise RuntimeError('call identity mismatch or legacy incomplete receipt; inspect retained artifacts, never redispatch')
        digest=saved.get('response_sha256')
        if digest is not None:
            if not output.is_file() or sha256_file(output)!=digest:
                raise RuntimeError('retained model response missing or changed')
        elif saved.get('returncode')==0 or output.exists():
            raise RuntimeError('response/receipt integrity mismatch')
        return saved
    events = output.with_suffix('.events.jsonl')
    if output.exists() or events.exists():
        raise RuntimeError('interrupted/existing call: reconcile it explicitly; never redispatch automatically')
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    allocation=json.loads((ROOT/'config/allocations.json').read_text())['per_phase'][phase]
    allowance=allocation.get('host_reasoning_job_timeout_s',600)
    if not 0 < timeout <= allowance:
        raise RuntimeError('model call exceeds recorded per-job host reasoning allowance')
    codex_binary = os.environ.get('CDRSI_CODEX_BIN', 'codex')
    reservation = reserve(ROOT, {'name': output.stem, 'phase': phase, 'model_calls': 1, 'binary': codex_binary,
                               'terminal_review': terminal, 'wall_s_max': timeout, 'model': 'gpt-6.1-sol',
                               'effort': effort, 'prompt_path': str(prompt_path), 'prompt_sha256': sha256_file(prompt_path)})
    argv = [codex_binary, 'exec', '--skip-git-repo-check', '--ephemeral', '-m', 'gpt-6.1-sol',
            '-c', f'model_reasoning_effort="{effort}"', '-s', 'read-only', '-C', str(ROOT.parent),
            '--json', '-o', str(output), '-']
    start = time.monotonic()
    timed_out = False
    launch_error = None
    returncode = None
    with events.open('x') as out, output.with_suffix('.stderr.txt').open('x') as err:
        try:
            proc = subprocess.Popen(['/usr/bin/time', '-l', *argv], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=out, stderr=err, text=True, start_new_session=True)
            try:
                proc.communicate(prompt_path.read_text(), timeout=timeout)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                timed_out = True
                os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                proc.wait()
            returncode = proc.returncode
        except OSError as exc:
            launch_error = str(exc)
            err.write(launch_error + '\n')
    usage = []
    for line in events.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            e = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if 'usage' in e:
            usage.append(e['usage'])
    stderr = output.with_suffix('.stderr.txt').read_text()
    rss = re.search(r'(\d+)\s+maximum resident set size', stderr)
    cpu = re.search(r'([\d.]+)\s+real\s+([\d.]+)\s+user\s+([\d.]+)\s+sys', stderr)
    if returncode == 0 and (not output.exists() or not output.read_text().strip()):
        launch_error = 'process returned success without a retained model response'
        returncode = 1
    result = {'prompt_sha256': sha256_file(prompt_path), 'returncode': returncode, 'timed_out': timed_out,
              'call_identity':identity,'response_sha256':sha256_file(output) if output.is_file() else None,
              'launch_error': launch_error,
              'wall_s': time.monotonic() - start, 'cpu_s': float(cpu[2]) + float(cpu[3]) if cpu else None,
              'peak_rss_bytes': int(rss[1]) if rss else None, 'tokens': usage or None,
              'actual_cost_usd': 0.0, 'host_model_cost_usd': 'unknown', 'output': str(output),
              'model': 'gpt-6.1-sol', 'effort': effort, 'reservation_id': reservation['record_id']}
    reconcile(ROOT, reservation['record_id'], {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != 'reservation_id'})
    append_record(ROOT / 'ledger/reviews.jsonl', {'kind': 'model_call', **result})
    receipt.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
    return result


if __name__ == '__main__':
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('prompt', type=Path); p.add_argument('output', type=Path)
    p.add_argument('--effort', choices=['high', 'xhigh'], required=True)
    p.add_argument('--phase', default='phase2_lock1'); p.add_argument('--terminal', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--timeout', type=int, default=600)
    args = p.parse_args()
    result = call(args.prompt, args.output, args.effort, args.phase, args.terminal, args.timeout)
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    raise SystemExit(0 if result['returncode'] == 0 and not result['timed_out'] else 1)

**0.5.1 Anatomy (`generations/{s,p}genNNN/`, never reused/overwritten).**
1. **SPEC.md + SHA-256 locked in ledger before any run:** discriminating question, candidate families, screen definition (incl. whether it is a *necessary-condition* screen — §0.5.2), battery definition, pass bar, stop rules, reserved battery budget. 2. **Enumerate** from the pool under frozen protocol; origins+parents per §0.4.4; legality validated.
3. **Screen (ranking only, labeled approximate).** Screen-positives are never claims.
4. **Recombine/refine winners** (`combination`/`refinement`); re-enter at screen; no score inheritance.

## 0. Operating rules (bind every phase)

### 0.1 Model routing & the frozen generator protocol (user-mandated)
| Role | Model | Effort | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Adversarial review of **everything** | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `high` | `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort='"high"' -s read-only` |
| Generation (candidates, challengers, summaries, extraction, unstick) | `gpt-6.1-sol` | `xhigh` | same, `xhigh`, sandbox per task |
| Lead investigator / statistics / implementation | Host agent | — | Local; all computation local |

- **Review protocol:** severity-tagged issues (low/medium/high/critical) with file:line evidence + one 0–100 score → lead verifies each (accept/reject with reason) → fix all verified → re-review until **≥ 90 and zero verified high/critical**. Transcripts + dispositions in `reviews/` + review ledger.
- **Generator-protocol freeze (isolates policy improvement):** for any policy comparison, the *entire* generation protocol is frozen and versioned — proposer prompt, direction-summary prompt, catalog-extraction prompt+schema, candidate ranking inputs, repair/unstick allowances, model IDs + efforts. Fixed arms run the **same protocol on their own admissible histories**. Any discretionary intervention outside the frozen protocol is logged as a **protocol breach**. The primary comparison is **assignment-retentive**: all assigned attempts, failures, and costs stay in their arm (no post-hoc exclusion of inconvenient outcomes). Exclusions are allowed **only** under predeclared, outcome-independent criteria frozen before the comparison. A breach that changes admissible information or treatment **invalidates the affected comparison** (restart requires appropriately unused evaluation evidence); logging/charging the breach never repairs biased inclusion. Only the executable **policy module** differs between arms.
- **Context/retrieval contract:** "exhaustive/full history" always means **exhaustive over the episode's admissible history** (§0.4.2 filter) — the same filter applies to *every* input channel: history index, retrieved records, rendered prompts, summaries, priorities, and unstick packets. Proposer inputs (token-bounded by construction; budgets frozen in the SPEC with reserved space for instructions + retrieved records): (a) **bounded directory header** — partition list with counts and ID ranges only (never a full ID dump), (b) **history index partitions** (fixed-size rows: ID, direction, origin, parents, outcome class, quality, cost), partitioned deterministically by direction and **sub-partitioned by fixed row/token caps so no partition — including one huge direction — exceeds its bound**, (c) episode-admissible catalog/frontier view, (d) direction summary, (e) full records via a **runner-mediated ID lookup** (proposer cites IDs or ID ranges; runner resolves partition→records deterministically, budgeted per generation, every lookup logged; cross-partition access always by ID). Complete addressability = every admissible ID is reachable via header→partition→lookup, without ever rendering the whole directory. **Overflow outcome:** if no legal rendering fits the frozen token budget, the generation call splits further (finer sub-partitions, header unchanged) — if still infeasible, the SPEC must narrow its index scope explicitly and the narrowing is ledgered; silent truncation is forbidden. Fixtures required: directory-alone-exceeds-cap and single-direction-exceeds-cap cases both rendering legally. What each call received is recorded in its input manifest. This is the single definition of "full tried history" used in GOAL.md. The hidden-outcome invariance test (§0.4.2) must cover the **complete rendered input and resulting decisions**, all channels included.
- Specialist roles stay distinct (novelty, provenance, modeling, evaluator, adversarial review). The evaluator gets a narrower interface than the proposer — a logged protocol, **not** a cryptographic boundary, never described as one.
- Every model call ledgered: model, effort, exact prompt (retained, §0.3), tokens when exposed, wall/CPU, peak RSS, cost or `unknown`. Additional metered API cap = **$0** unless user-configured; unmeasurable material cost ⇒ C9 all-in savings uncertifiable (Phase 5).
